note: Selective Nav1.7 blockers tested in small crossover studies of SCN9A-mutation erythromelalgia: funapide (XEN402/XPF-001, oral and topical) 2010-2012 and PF-05089771 2012-2013; none advanced past phase 2.
label: Inherited erythromelalgia (Nav1.7 blockers)

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Sci Transl Med paywalled; Firecrawl returned abstract and references only).
engagement.note: PF-05089771 reversed hyperexcitability in patient iPSC sensory neurons; neuronal excitability was not measured in the dosed patients.
engagement.quote: The in vitro IEM phenotype was sensitive to Nav1.7 blockers, including the clinical test agent.
engagement.judgement: The model's PD readout (firing/heat responses of sensory neurons) has no counterpart in the trial, which recorded pain scores and PK only; no microneurography or skin-biopsy readout was found.

dose.confidence_note: Cao 2016 body not read (paywalled); a dose rationale may sit in its methods or supplement. Funapide (XEN402 400 mg BID) dose rationale also not found.
dose.note: Patients got one 1600 mg oral dose per session; no published model stated an exposure or Nav1.7 block target for it.
dose.quote: A single oral dose of PF-05089771 1600 mg solution to be administered on Day 1 of each treatment session.
dose.judgement: Dated with the iPSC model's first publication (2016). The sponsor's dose is not a model-stated target, so untested. McDermott 2023 (Brain, doi:10.1093/brain/awac031) later estimated ~50% Nav1.7 block reverses IEM iPSC hyperexcitability with no member drug, so it is not scored here.

dose.population: No patients compared at the opener; track run for PF-05089771 ahead of IEM use
dose.confidence_note: Opening year is a proxy: the microdose study NCT01165736 started 2010-07; the PBPK prediction was made before the SAD study (NCT01259882, 2010-12). Abstract-level.
dose.judgement: Opening entry at the model's first use; the prediction was not public until 2016.
dose.quote: A physiologically-based PK (PBPK) model was used to predict exposure and multiples of Nav1.7 50 % inhibitory concentration (IC50) for each compound at higher doses.
dose.note: PBPK model built on microdose PK predicted the oral dose giving about 12x Nav1.7 IC50 at Cmax for PF-05089771.
dose.model: PBPK model from a human IV/oral microdose study (PF-05089771)

dose.magnitude_basis: PBPK-predicted vs observed plasma exposure of PF-05089771 in the single ascending oral dose study
dose.population: Healthy volunteers (single ascending oral dose study NCT01259882)
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Springer full text not retrieved), so the fold error behind 'compared well' is unknown and magnitude is null. SAD registry NCT01259882 has no posted results found. IEM-patient exposure versus the IC50 multiple not checked (Cao 2016 paywalled).
dose.judgement: Healthy-volunteer PK counts for dose. The PBPK model stated an exposure target (12x IC50 at Cmax with 1 g); the SAD study, run after the prediction, matched it, and IEM patients then got 1600 mg, above the predicted 1 g. Reaching target is scored here; whether it worked is efficacy.
dose.quote: In a subsequent single ascending oral dose clinical study, the predictions for PF-05089771 compared well with observed data.
dose.note: Single ascending oral doses in volunteers matched the PBPK exposure predictions; the IEM trial then dosed 1600 mg.
dose.model: PBPK model from a human IV/oral microdose study (PF-05089771)

efficacy.model: SCN9A human genetics (loss-of-function CIP, gain-of-function IEM)
efficacy.note: Loss-of-function SCN9A nonsense mutations abolish pain, predicting that Nav1.7 blockade would relieve Nav1.7 gain-of-function pain. Opens the genetics track for oral funapide (XPF-001/XEN402).
efficacy.quote: Our data suggest that SCN9A is an essential and non-redundant requirement for nociception in humans.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry: the class went into IEM patients on human genetics, not a disease animal model; gain-of-function IEM variants (2004) plus loss-of-function CIP (2006) are the model system, no member drug involved.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: pain after heat/exercise induction, XEN402 vs placebo (42% less)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Pain full text not retrieved). n=4 crossover, 2-day periods. NCT01090622 (first posted 2010-03-22) has no posted results.
efficacy.model: SCN9A human genetics (loss-of-function CIP, gain-of-function IEM)
efficacy.note: Oral funapide (XEN402) 400 mg BID cut induced pain 42% versus placebo in 4 SCN9A-mutation IEM patients, as the genetics predicted. Randomised 2-period crossover, oral funapide alone.
efficacy.quote: XEN402 increased the time to maximal pain induction and significantly reduced the amount of pain (42% less) after induction (P=.014).
efficacy.judgement: The paper itself sets the CIP/IEM 'opposite phenotype' genetics beside the result (stated comparison); Goldberg 2012 Clin Genet (doi:10.1111/j.1399-0004.2012.01942.x) restates it. Endpoint role set to primary on the abstract's 'primary aim'; the registry outcome wording was not checked. XPF-001 is a code name for funapide. The topical funapide and PF-05089771 trials formerly listed in patient_trials are now their own tracks (appended entries).

efficacy.magnitude_basis: in-vitro reversal of IEM neuron hyperexcitability vs heat-induced pain in the same patients
efficacy.population: SCN9A mutation-confirmed inherited erythromelalgia, PF-05089771 crossover (NCT01769274)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Registry primary (PI-NRS 0-4 h) means 2.08 vs 2.73 and 1.95 vs 2.04 on drug vs placebo, no inferential test posted.
efficacy.note: Neurons derived from four trial participants reproduced the IEM phenotype and its sensitivity to PF-05089771; most patients' heat-induced pain fell. Retrodiction: the result came from the same trial's patients, public with or before the neurons.
efficacy.short: Trial patients' neurons reproduced the response
efficacy.quote: The in vitro IEM phenotype was sensitive to Nav1.7 blockers, including the clinical test agent.
efficacy.judgement: Scored as a retrodiction: the lines were derived from the trial's own subjects (trial completed 2013-07) and published with the result, so the neurons did not predict it. The patient-level comparison was phenotype severity vs excitability ('trend toward a correlation'), not drug response, so prediction_level stays class.

efficacy.population: Primary or inherited erythromelalgia, topical funapide (XPF-002) trial NCT01486446; SCN9A genotype not an entry criterion
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract read (Europe PMC); opener year is a proxy (trial start).
efficacy.model: SCN9A human genetics (loss-of-function CIP, gain-of-function IEM)
efficacy.note: Opens the SCN9A genetics track for funapide (topical); the genetics predicted relief before NCT01486446 started (Primary or inherited erythromelalgia (topical XPF-002 trial NCT01486446)).
efficacy.quote: Our data suggest that SCN9A is an essential and non-redundant requirement for nociception in humans.
efficacy.judgement: Track opener at the model's first use for funapide by the topical route, dated by the start of its first IEM trial (NCT01486446, Primary or inherited erythromelalgia (topical XPF-002 trial NCT01486446)); the genetics model itself dates from 2006.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: mean daily cooling uses, drug vs placebo
efficacy.population: Primary or inherited erythromelalgia, topical funapide (XPF-002) trial NCT01486446; SCN9A genotype not an entry criterion
efficacy.confidence_note: Registry results only; no publication found. n=8 (1 placebo), no inferential test. SCN9A genotype not required for entry, so the biomarker share is unknown.
efficacy.model: SCN9A human genetics (loss-of-function CIP, gain-of-function IEM)
efficacy.note: Topical funapide 8% ointment: 0.24 vs 2.4 cooling uses/day (7 drug, 1 placebo), as genetics predicted. Exploratory design, no primary endpoint or success bar; scored in the predicted direction (single-arm ruling).
efficacy.quote: A smaller average number of cooling uses each day in Treatment Period 2 indicates that subjects were in less pain/required less use of cooling to relieve their EM pain and vice versa.
efficacy.judgement: Registry states 'There was no primary outcome measure'; the posted first-listed measure (daily cooling uses) is scored in the direction the genetics predicted, as for a single-arm trial with no success bar. Paired with Cox 2006 (comparison not stated in the record).

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract read (Europe PMC); opener year is a proxy (trial start).
efficacy.model: SCN9A human genetics (loss-of-function CIP, gain-of-function IEM)
efficacy.note: Opens the SCN9A genetics track for pf-05089771 (oral); the genetics predicted relief before NCT01769274 started (SCN9A mutation-confirmed inherited erythromelalgia (NCT01769274)).
efficacy.quote: Our data suggest that SCN9A is an essential and non-redundant requirement for nociception in humans.
efficacy.judgement: Track opener at the model's first use for pf-05089771 by the oral route, dated by the start of its first IEM trial (NCT01769274, SCN9A mutation-confirmed inherited erythromelalgia (NCT01769274)); the genetics model itself dates from 2006.

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Sci Transl Med paywalled). Registry primary posted 2019-11-19 without an inferential test.
efficacy.model: SCN9A human genetics (loss-of-function CIP, gain-of-function IEM)
efficacy.note: Single 1600 mg oral PF-05089771 lowered heat-induced pain in most of 5 IEM patients, as the genetics predicted; registry PI-NRS 0-4 h 2.08 vs 2.73 and 1.95 vs 2.04.
efficacy.short: PF-05089771 eased IEM pain in most
efficacy.quote: Five patients with IEM were treated with a new potent and selective compound that blocked the Nav1.7 sodium channel resulting in a decrease in heat-induced pain in most of the patients.
efficacy.reason: Most patients' pain fell on drug
efficacy.judgement: Paired with Cox 2006 (the trial paper does not set the CIP genetics beside the result in the abstract). Partial: most, not all, patients responded and session 2 means barely differ; dated by the 2016 paper, before the 2019 registry posting.

patient_trials.quote: A single oral dose of PF-05089771 1600 mg solution to be administered on Day 1 of each treatment session.

safety.confidence_note: No FDA/EMA review exists (no NDA); registry AE table read: 0 serious AEs on PF-05089771 (NCT01769274).
safety.note: No serious adverse events on PF-05089771 in the IEM trial (0/5); its animal toxicology and stated margins are not public.
safety.quote: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the efficacy and safety of single doses of PF-05089771 against placebo in treatment of pain in patients with primary, inherited erythromelalgia.
safety.judgement: Sole entry is the opener at the model's first use (2010, proxy), per check adjudication under rule 6; no public stated harm or margin, so the track stays untested.

safety.confidence_note: Abstract read; no Xenon preclinical paper found. Opener year is the first IEM trial start (NCT01090622, 2010-04).
safety.note: Oral funapide given to 4 IEM patients; no preclinical toxicology or stated margin for funapide is public.
safety.quote: In each treatment period (2days), separated by a 2-day washout period, patients were orally administered XEN402 (400mg twice daily) or matching placebo.
safety.judgement: Split from the shared toxicology entry: funapide oral is its own track. Toxicology unpublished, so untested.

safety.population: Primary or inherited erythromelalgia, topical funapide (XPF-002) trial NCT01486446
safety.confidence_note: Registry AE table read (results posted 2014-04-14): 1/7 serious AE on XPF-002. Opener year is the trial start (2011-12).
safety.note: Topical funapide: 1 serious adverse event in 7 patients; no dermal or systemic toxicology for the ointment is public.
safety.quote: Phase 2a, Exploratory Study to Evaluate the Safety, Efficacy, Tolerability and Pharmacokinetics of XPF-002 in Patients With Primary/Inherited Erythromelalgia
safety.judgement: Split from the shared toxicology entry: funapide topical is its own track. Toxicology unpublished, so untested.
